subject: [AMBER] Raw RDF exceeds total number of waters?

messages.author: Matthew Guberman-Pfeffer
messages.body:
Dear Amber Community,
The below CPPTRAJ command gives me raw RDF values that exceed the number of waters in the simulation box:
radial out rdf.dat 0.1 15 :WAT,Na+ :1280 density 0.033456 intrdf intrdf.dat rawrdf rawrdf.dat bymol1
Is it an imaging issue?
What I’m really concerned about is the same command run on two different trajectories with identical counts of WAT and Na+ gives me raw RDF values that almost systematically differ by a factor of ~2. The only difference between the simulations is the temperature. I need to know if the difference is real.
Best,
Matthew

messages.author: Daniel Roe
messages.body:
Hi,
Unless I misunderstand you, you are selecting both water and sodium, so the
count should exceed the number of waters, right?
-Dan

messages.author: Daniel Roe
messages.body:
Hi,
Sorry for the delay on this. The answer is pretty straightforward
actually - the "raw" RDF is literally that - just the total bin
counts, so if you're doing more than one frame you'll easily get more
than the total number of waters in the system. Try it on a single
frame to see what I mean. Hope this helps,
-Dan
